title: Minimum Operations to Make Array Modulo Alternating II
summary: Given an integer array nums and an integer k, determine the least number of operations needed to adjust each element by +1 or -1 so that the array becomes modulo alternating.
statement: Given an integer array nums and an integer k, determine the least number of operations needed to adjust each element by +1 or -1 so that the array becomes modulo alternating. A modulo alternating array has two distinct integers x and y (0 <= x, y < k) where for even indices, nums[i] % k equals x, and for odd indices, nums[i] % k equals y.
constraints: nums is nonempty and k is at least two.
One operation adds or subtracts one from one element; residues wrap modulo k.
Choose distinct target residues for even and odd indices and minimize all operations.
hints: Changing an integer residue has circular distance min(|a-b|,k-|a-b|).
For one parity, represent every residue by its unique shifted copy inside a length-k window around each target.
Sorted shifted residues and prefix sums compute every target cost in O(k log n).
Combine each even target with the cheapest odd target having a different residue; only the two cheapest odd choices are needed.
editorial: Combine each even target with the cheapest odd target having a different residue; only the two cheapest odd choices are needed.

tests.explanation: Moving the odd-index value four to residue two and the even-index value two to residue one costs two operations total.
One parity can stay at residue one while the other moves to residue zero, costing one operation.
